title: Decoding the Most Common Retailer Deduction Codes and How to Dispute Them
summary: Learn how retail suppliers decode deduction reason codes, gather required proof, dispute invalid claims, and prevent recurring revenue loss.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


How to decode common deduction reasons across major retail and distribution channels


-


The essential documentation required to build winning dispute cases


-


Strategies for root-cause analysis to prevent recurring valid deductions from eroding margins


Every month, finance and accounts receivable teams across the supply chain encounter invoice remittances that arrive for significantly less than the billed amount. A portion of expected payment has vanished, accompanied by a cryptic string of numbers or letters.


Deductions are automated financial adjustments triggered when a buying org identifies an error in the order-to-cash process. Regardless of product category, volume, and operational complexity, these charges can quietly erode revenue.


Despite the margin erosion, industry data indicates that suppliers rarely dispute retailer deductions. Disputing invalid deductions can result in revenue recovery for suppliers, but many finance teams lack the visibility, time, and documentation needed to evaluate every code before dispute windows close.


Understanding deduction codes is the first step toward reclaiming lost revenue. A deduction code is a diagnostic tool that indicates what the operational gap was that created it, and indicates whether a charge is disputable.


**Related Reading** :[What Is Remittance Advice and Why Is It Important for Suppliers?](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-remittance-advice-and-why-is-it-important-for-suppliers)


## Decoding Common Deduction Codes by Category


Retailers and distributors use distinct taxonomies, but most deduction codes fall into four core operational families. Recognizing what these codes represent allows AR teams to gather the precise evidence needed for a dispute.


### 1. Shortages, Overages, and Damages (OS&D)


Shortage claims represent the largest share of deductions across retail and wholesale distribution. Shortages occur when a retailer's receiving count is lower than the quantity listed on the invoice.


-


[Walmart](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/unlock-your/deduction-codes-explained-guide) **:** Uses Code 22 (goods billed not shipped), Code 24 (carton shortage), and Code 25 (no merchandise received for invoice). Code 22 is frequently triggered when an advance ship notice (ASN) is missing or transmitted late.


-


[Target](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/unlock-your/target-deductions-explained) **:** Uses Code A030 for carton shortages and Code A034 for unit shortages.


-


[Amazon](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/unlock-your/amazon-deduction-explained) **:** Categorizes shortages under Purchase Quantity Variance (PQV) or remaining shortages when physical receiving records do not match invoice data.


-


[Distributors](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/disputing-distributor-deductions-and-chargebacks) **:** Sysco groups these under Overages, Shortages, and Damages (OS&D), while KeHE assesses a $0.29 per-unit fee on unsaleable items.


### 2. Pricing Discrepancies and Cost Differences


Pricing deductions occur when the unit cost on the invoice does not match the purchase order (PO) or the price active in the retailer's system.


-


**Walmart:** Uses Code 10 (price difference as documented) and Code 11 (pricing overcharge)


-


**Target:** Uses Code A036 (cost difference)


-


**UNFI:** Uses codes like HCG (cost of goods) for conventional accounts or discrepancy suffixes for natural accounts


### 3. Compliance and Shipping Violations


Compliance fines are assessed when a shipment breaches operational, transportation, or packaging standards.


-


**Walmart:** Tracks delivery timing through[on-time in-full (OTIF)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/unlock-your/the-ultimate-guide-to-otif) (Code 99), fining suppliers 3% of the cost of goods sold on non-compliant shipments. Walmart also enforces the[Supplier Quality Excellence Program (SQEP)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/supplier-guided-checklist-walmart-sqep) for PO accuracy, barcode, and packaging defects.


-


[Target](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/navigating-targets-compliance-policies-a-complete-overview) **:** Enforces the Perfect Order Program, issuing automated chargebacks (Code A176) for late arrivals or fill-rate failures.


-


**Department stores:** Belk issues chargebacks for unapproved hangers or missing RFID tags,[Nordstrom](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/supplier-compliance-at-nordstrom) assesses $150 per incident for UPC catalog errors, and Macy's penalizes missing GS1-128 barcodes.


**Related Reading** :[An Overview of Apparel Compliance Deductions](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/an-overview-of-apparel-compliance-deductions)


### 4. Trade Allowances and Co-Op Agreements


Unlike compliance fines, allowances represent pre-negotiated commercial terms that usually apply to promotions or allowances.


-


Amazon terms these[Co-Op or Contra CoGS](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/unlock-your/amazon-co-op-cheat-sheet) , covering promotional, freight, and damage allowances.


-


Walmart uses allowance codes 10 through 19 and 40 through 59 for promotional and markdown terms.


-


In department stores, allowances cover seasonal markdowns and cooperative advertising.


Invalid allowance deductions occur when a retailer deducts an allowance twice or applies terms outside the agreed contract period.


## Triaging Deductions: Valid vs. Invalid


A successful deduction management program relies on fast, accurate triage. Attempting to dispute every deduction without checking validity wastes effort and strains retailer relationships. Conversely, writing off every charge guarantees permanent revenue loss.


Most deductions fall into three classifications:


-


**Invalid deductions:** Charges imposed by the retailer in error. Examples include claiming a shortage when the shipment arrived complete, applying a price reduction after a cost increase was approved in writing, or issuing duplicate chargebacks. Invalid deductions require immediate dispute filing for revenue recovery.


-


**Valid planned deductions:** Contractual allowances, such as promotional discounts or agreed trade terms. These are legitimate costs that should be audited against the vendor agreement and budgeted accordingly.


-


**Valid unplanned deductions:** Charges resulting from actual supplier errors, such as a late shipment, an unscannable barcode, or an unfulfilled case count. While these claims cannot be disputed, they are fixable. Every valid deduction highlights a process breakdown in manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, or EDI mapping.


**Related Reading** :[Glossary of Common Deduction Terms](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/glossary-of-common-deduction-terms)


## Building the Dispute Evidence Kit and Navigating Vendor Portals


When disputing an invalid deduction, your claim is only as strong as your supporting documentation. Retailers evaluate disputes based on objective proof.


### The Essential Evidence Kit


For most shortage, pricing, and compliance disputes, suppliers must compile a complete documentation trail:


1.


[Purchase order (PO)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-a-purchase-order) **:** Demonstrates the original quantities, SKUs, and unit costs agreed upon.


1.


[Bill of lading (BOL)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/bill-lading-bol-supplypike) **:** A clean, signed BOL proves that the carrier picked up the complete order from your facility.


1.


[Proof of delivery (POD)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-proof-of-delivery) **:** This document is a delivery receipt signed by a retailer representative that confirms arrival.


1.


[Advance ship notice (ASN)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-856-ship-notice-manifest) **:** A timestamped EDI 856 records that electronic data was transmitted before delivery.


1.


**Supplier invoice:** Shows the exact items and prices billed to the retailer.


Depending on the deduction or chargeback, selling orgs may need to provide more specific dispute documentation like images provided by the shipper or the retailer in the case of certain compliance deductions.


### Retailer Portal Rules and Timelines


Larger retailers generally process disputes in portals with strict deadlines and requirements:


-


[Walmart](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/walmart-apdp-portal-explained-best-practices) **:** Disputes for AP deductions are managed in[Retail Link](https://retaillink.login.wal-mart.com/?resumePath=/as/EmaQECQP8i/resume/as/authorization.ping) through the Accounts Payable Disputes Portal (APDP). The dispute window is generally 180 days from the charge date.


-


[Target](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/the-target-portal) **:** Uses Synergy in[Partners Online for AP deductions](https://logonservices.oauth.iam.partnersonline.com/login/responses/logoff.html) . Collect shipment disputes must be submitted within 9 months, while general claims must be filed within 18 months of the remittance date. Target restricts suppliers to three dispute attempts per charge before assessing fines on subsequent tries.


-


[Amazon](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/unlock-your/amazon-deduction-explained) **:** Disputes are processed via[Vendor Central](https://vendorcentral.amazon.com/ap/signin?clientContext=134-4298797-1976426&openid.pape.preferred_auth_policies=SinglefactorWithPossessionChallenge&openid.return_to=https://vendorcentral.amazon.com/&openid.identity=http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0/identifier_select&openid.assoc_handle=amzn_vc_us_v2&openid.mode=checkid_setup&intercept=false&language=en_US&openid.claimed_id=http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0/identifier_select&pageId=amzn_vc_us_auth&openid.ns=http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0) under Dispute Management. Line-item backup reports become available on the seventh day of each month.


-


**Distributors & department stores:**


-


UNFI[conventional suppliers](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-conventional-suppliers-dispute-unfi-deductions) manage claims in[ePASS](https://suppliers.unfi.com/Account/Login) within 60 days, while UNFI[natural suppliers](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-natural-suppliers-dispute-unfi-deductions) submit dispute forms via email.


-


KeHE disputes are researched in K-Solve within[KeHE CONNECT](https://connect-identity-server.kehe.com/Account/Login?ReturnUrl=/connect/authorize/callback?client_id=connect-supplier-web&redirect_uri=https://connectsupplier.kehe.com/callback&response_type=code&scope=openid%20profile%20vendor-pricing-mgmt-api%20power-bi-report-api%20customer-api%20kehe-api&state=750af18892074e2ba65221857403ff73&code_challenge=vn7HviDPk17egiZY__M6hsSBDK0BcrgbzN67R9Kn2U0&code_challenge_method=S256) .


-


[Macy's](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/macys-and-bloomingdales-accounts-payable-disputing-and-deductions-types) requires disputes to be submitted through[Macysnet](https://login.macys.net/sso/XUI/?realm=/vendor&spEntityID=vendorportal.gke.prod.sp&service=5vendor-mgt-system&goto=https://login.macys.net:443/sso/saml2/continue/metaAlias/vendor/vmp?secondVisitUrl=/sso/SSORedirect/metaAlias/vendor/vmp?ReqID=_8f2db4cfe234a22a0d54&AMAuthCookie=#login/) within 60 days.


Acting within the first 48 hours of receiving a remittance is critical. Gathering carrier affidavits, shipping logs, and warehouse photos becomes significantly harder as time passes.


## Root-Cause Prevention: Stopping Repeat Losses


Disputing invalid deductions recovers past revenue, but root-cause prevention protects future margins. A mature program connects AR findings to operational teams.


To stop recurring charges:


1.


**Centralize deduction data:** Log every deduction code, dollar amount, retailer, distribution center, and carrier into a single tracking system.


1.


**Assign operational owners:** Route ASN errors to IT/EDI, labeling errors to warehouse operations, routing fines to transportation, and price differences to master data management.


1.


**Track key metrics:** Monitor dispute recovery rate, average resolution time, and the recurrence rate of specific deduction codes after operational fixes are applied.
